---
layout: default
title: GCSE maths question bank
description: Search real Edexcel GCSE maths past paper questions by tier, paper, strand and sub-strand. View them on screen or print them straight into a worksheet.
permalink: /gcse-question-bank/
body_class: page-gcse-question-bank
---

<div id="gqb-page">
<style>
  :root{
    --blue:#1c75bc;      /* Number */
    --green:#009444;     /* Algebra */
    --purple:#800080;    /* Statistics */
    --orange:#f7941e;    /* Geometry and measures */
    --amber:#a15c1f;      /* NEW: Ratio, proportion and rates of change - needs sign-off */
    --rose:#c43d6b;      /* NEW: Probability - needs sign-off */
    --navy:#0f1120;
    --bg:#f5f6f8;
    --card-border:#e5e7eb;
    --text:#20222b;
    --muted:#6b7280;
  }
  *{box-sizing:border-box;}
  body{
    margin:0;
    background:var(--bg);
    font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif;
    font-weight:300;
    color:var(--text);
    transition:padding-bottom .2s ease;
  }
  h1,h2,h3,h4,button,.btn{font-weight:700;}
  .wrap{max-width:1100px;margin:0 auto;padding:0 20px;}

  /* Filter rail — scrolls with the page, no sticky positioning */
  .filters{
    background:#fff;
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--card-border);
    padding:14px 0;
  }
  .filter-row{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:24px;align-items:center;}
  .filter-group{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:5px;}
  .filter-label{font-size:.72rem;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.06em;color:var(--muted);font-weight:700;}

  .tier-toggle{display:flex;border:1px solid var(--card-border);border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;}
  .tier-toggle button{
    border:none;background:#fff;color:var(--text);padding:8px 14px;font-size:.85rem;cursor:pointer;
    border-right:1px solid var(--card-border);white-space:nowrap;
  }
  .tier-toggle button:last-child{border-right:none;}
  .tier-toggle button.active{background:var(--navy);color:#fff;}

  .chip-row{display:flex;flex-wrap:nowrap;justify-content:space-between;gap:8px;overflow-x:auto;padding-bottom:4px;flex:1;}
  .chip-row::-webkit-scrollbar{height:5px;}
  .chip-row::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb{background:var(--card-border);border-radius:3px;}
  .chip{
    border:2px solid var(--chip-color,var(--card-border));background:#fff;border-radius:8px;
    padding:7px 14px;font-size:.83rem;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;color:var(--chip-color,var(--text));
    white-space:nowrap;flex-shrink:0;transition:background .12s ease,color .12s ease;
  }
  .chip.active{background:var(--chip-color,var(--navy));color:#fff;}

  select, input[type="text"]{
    font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif;font-weight:400;
    border:1px solid var(--card-border);border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;font-size:.85rem;
    min-width:200px;background:#fff;color:var(--text);
  }
  input[type="text"]:focus{outline:none;border-color:var(--orange);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--orange);}
  input[type="text"][readonly]:focus{border-color:var(--card-border);box-shadow:none;}

  .combobox{position:relative;display:flex;align-items:stretch;}
  .combobox input[type="text"]{width:100%;min-width:0;padding-right:62px;}
  .combobox-arrow{
    position:absolute;right:2px;top:0;bottom:0;width:32px;
    border:none;background:none;color:var(--muted);cursor:pointer;font-size:1.3rem;
  }
  .combobox-arrow:hover{color:var(--text);}
  .combobox-clear{
    position:absolute;right:26px;top:0;bottom:0;width:26px;
    border:none;background:none;color:var(--muted);cursor:pointer;font-size:.85rem;
  }
  .combobox-clear:hover{color:var(--orange);}
  .combobox-clear.hidden{display:none;}

  .search-suggestions{
    position:absolute;top:100%;left:0;right:0;margin-top:4px;
    background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--card-border);border-radius:8px;
    box-shadow:0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.12);z-index:30;overflow:hidden;
    max-height:320px;overflow-y:auto;
  }
  .search-suggestions.hidden{display:none;}
  .search-suggestion{
    padding:10px 14px;font-size:.9rem;cursor:pointer;border-bottom:1px solid var(--bg);
  }
  .search-suggestion:last-child{border-bottom:none;}
  .search-suggestion:hover,.search-suggestion.highlighted{background:#fde2e2;}

  .results-meta{padding:14px 0 4px;font-size:.85rem;color:var(--muted);}

  /* Question grid */
  .grid{
    display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr);gap:16px;
    padding:10px 0 100px;
  }
  @media (max-width:760px){.grid{grid-template-columns:1fr;}}

  .card{
    background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--card-border);border-radius:10px;
    border-left:4px solid var(--strand,#999);
    padding:16px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:10px;cursor:pointer;
    transition:box-shadow .15s ease;
    height:300px;overflow-x:hidden;overflow-y:hidden;min-width:0;
  }
  .card:hover{box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.08);}
  /* No static padding-top here on purpose - see fixExpClipping() in the
     script. A superscript/fraction on a card's first line can clip against
     this container's own overflow:hidden top edge (transform moves paint
     position, not the layout box), but the fix is measured and applied
     per-card in JS after each render, only when that card actually needs
     it - a flat CSS value here previously added visible space to every
     card, including the vast majority with nothing near their top edge. */
  .card-body{flex:1;min-height:0;overflow-x:hidden;overflow-y:hidden;position:relative;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;min-width:0;}
  .card-body::after{
    content:"";position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;height:36px;
    background:linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(255,255,255,0), #fff);
    pointer-events:none;
  }
  .card-top{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-start;gap:8px;}
  .source-tag{font-size:.72rem;color:var(--muted);}
  .marks-badge{
    font-size:.72rem;font-weight:700;background:var(--bg);border:1px solid var(--card-border);
    border-radius:20px;padding:3px 9px;white-space:nowrap;
  }
  .subtopic-pill{
    align-self:flex-start;font-size:.72rem;font-weight:700;color:#fff;
    background:var(--strand,#999);border-radius:6px;padding:3px 9px;
  }
  .q-heading{margin:0;font-size:.95rem;}
  .q-text{font-size:.88rem;line-height:1.5;font-weight:400;white-space:pre-line;flex:0 0 auto;}
  .q-diagram{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;justify-content:center;padding:6px 0 14px;flex:0 0 auto;min-width:0;max-width:100%;}
  .q-diagram img{min-width:0;}
  /* Cropped-from-PDF questions: shown left-aligned at a fixed 0.5x of their
     native pixel size (never stretched to fill the card), with no
     "Question N" heading since the number is already baked into the crop. */
  .q-diagram.q-crop{justify-content:flex-start;padding:2px 0 14px;}
  .q-diagram.q-crop img{display:block;margin:0;height:auto;}
  /* Modal has far more horizontal room than a grid card, so its crop uses a
     larger fixed scale (not the grid's 0.5x) - but still a FIXED multiple
     of native size, not stretched to the container. Stretching to width:100%
     made every crop's on-screen text a different size depending on that
     crop's own aspect ratio, which is exactly what a fixed scale avoids. */
  .q-diagram.q-crop-modal{display:block;padding:6px 0 16px;}
  .q-diagram.q-crop-modal img{display:block;max-width:100%;height:auto;margin:0;}
  /* A part without its own baked-in number (e.g. part (b) onwards) gets
     just the bare question number ("8", not "8(b)") to its left, in the
     exam paper's own bold serif style, matching the numerals that ARE
     baked into the crop images. */
  .q-part-row{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:8px;}
  .q-part-number{flex:0 0 auto;font-family:'Times New Roman',Georgia,serif;font-weight:700;line-height:1.3;font-variant-numeric:lining-nums;font-feature-settings:"lnum" 1;}
  /* Algebra letters need the genuine curled serif italic seen on the actual
     exam papers (e.g. Times New Roman Italic) - a sans-serif italic like DM
     Sans just slants the upright letterform and never gets that curled
     shape, regardless of whether a true italic weight is loaded. Maths
     notation (fractions, exponents, vector arrows) is switched to the same
     serif stack throughout so numerals match the papers too, not just the
     italic letters. */
  .q-text em, .answer-box em, .print-answers em{
    font-family:'Times New Roman',Times,'Liberation Serif',serif;font-style:italic;
  }
  .frac{display:inline-flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;vertical-align:middle;font-size:.92em;line-height:1.15;text-align:center;margin:0 2px;position:relative;top:.1em;font-family:'Times New Roman',Times,'Liberation Serif',serif;}
  .frac-sm{display:inline-flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;vertical-align:middle;font-size:.72em;line-height:.95;text-align:center;margin:0 1px;font-family:'Times New Roman',Times,'Liberation Serif',serif;}
  /* Every previous attempt at raising the exponent relied on vertical-align
     or baseline-alignment behaviour (native <sup>, position:relative on an
     inline-flex box, vertical-align on an inline-block) - all of which
     depend on how a browser computes an element's baseline, which is
     exactly the part that's been unreliable across attempts. transform is
     different in kind: it's a plain geometric shift applied after layout
     is resolved, with no baseline computation involved at all, so there's
     nothing left for a browser to interpret differently.
  */
  .exp{
    display:inline-block;font-size:.68em;line-height:1;
    font-family:'Times New Roman',Times,'Liberation Serif',serif;
    transform:translateY(-1.1em);
  }
  .exp .frac{top:0;}
  /* Vector arrows are drawn as a small inline SVG rather than CSS
     pseudo-elements with absolute positioning. Every previous attempt at
     the latter depended on how a browser resolves an absolutely-positioned
     element's containing block inside a nested inline-block, which turned
     out to behave unpredictably. An SVG's internal coordinates are fixed
     and rendered identically everywhere - there's no positioning
     ambiguity left for a browser to get wrong.
  */
  /* The arrow needs to sit above the letters, purely as a decoration, with
     the letters themselves behaving as ordinary inline text so they align
     to the surrounding sentence's baseline exactly like plain text would -
     that ordinary alignment is unambiguous and reliable, unlike flexbox's
     baseline synthesis for a column-direction container (which browsers
     resolve inconsistently: they variously use the first child, the last
     child, or the container's own margin edge, so the letters would end up
     floating off the baseline depending on the browser). Taking the arrow
     out of the flow entirely with absolute positioning sidesteps that: the
     letters are the only thing left participating in normal text flow, so
     there's nothing left for a browser to disagree about.
  */
  .vec{position:relative;display:inline-block;padding-top:9px;margin:0 1px;font-family:'Times New Roman',Times,'Liberation Serif',serif;}
  .vec svg{position:absolute;top:0;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);width:1.5em;height:.5em;}
  .radicand{border-top:1.5px solid currentColor;padding:0 2px;}
  .frac .num{border-bottom:1px solid currentColor;padding:0 3px;}
  .frac .den{padding:0 3px;}
  .frac-sm .num{border-bottom:1px solid currentColor;padding:0 2px;}
  .frac-sm .den{padding:0 2px;}
  .card-actions{
    margin-top:auto;padding-top:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--card-border);
    display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;
  }
  .add-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;font-size:.82rem;cursor:pointer;}
  .print-one{
    border:none;background:none;color:var(--blue);font-size:.8rem;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
    display:flex;align-items:center;gap:4px;
  }
  .print-one:hover{text-decoration:underline;}

  /* Sticky worksheet builder bar - the signature element */
  .builder-bar{
    position:fixed;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;z-index:30;
    background:var(--navy);color:#fff;
    padding:14px 0;
    transform:translateY(110%);transition:transform .25s ease;
    box-shadow:0 -6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.15);
  }
  .builder-bar.show{transform:translateY(0);}
  .builder-bar .wrap{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px;}
  .builder-info{font-size:.9rem;}
  .builder-info strong{color:var(--orange);}
  .builder-actions{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:center;}
  .builder-left{display:flex;gap:14px;align-items:center;}
  .answers-toggle-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;font-size:.85rem;color:#fff;white-space:nowrap;cursor:pointer;}
  .print-answers{display:none;}
  .btn{
    border:none;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 16px;font-size:.85rem;cursor:pointer;
  }
  .btn-primary{background:var(--orange);color:#0f1120;}
  .btn-primary:hover{background:#d97e0f;}
  .btn-ghost{background:transparent;color:#fff;border:1px solid #454863;}
  .btn-ghost:hover{background:#1c1e33;}

  .no-results{padding:60px 0;text-align:center;color:var(--muted);}
  .load-more-wrap{display:flex;justify-content:center;padding:8px 0 40px;margin-top:-72px;}
  .btn-loadmore{background:var(--navy);color:#fff;border:none;font-weight:700;}
  .btn-loadmore:hover{background:#1c1e33;}
  .load-more-wrap .btn{padding:12px 28px;}

  /* Question viewer modal */
  .modal-overlay{
    position:fixed;inset:0;background:rgba(15,17,32,.55);z-index:50;
    display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;padding:24px 16px;
  }
  .modal-overlay.hidden{display:none;}
  .modal-box{
    background:#fff;border-radius:12px;max-width:880px;width:100%;
    height:min(85vh,720px);
    position:relative;border-left:6px solid var(--strand,#999);
    display:flex;flex-direction:column;
    overflow:hidden;
  }
  .modal-header{
    padding:20px 50px 14px 24px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--card-border);flex-shrink:0;
  }
  .modal-header-top{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:14px;}
  .modal-scroll-body{overflow-y:auto;flex:1;min-height:0;padding:18px 24px;}
  #modalContent{display:flex;flex-direction:column;height:100%;min-height:0;gap:10px;padding-top:4px;}
  .modal-close{
    position:absolute;top:16px;right:18px;border:none;background:none;
    font-size:1.3rem;cursor:pointer;color:var(--muted);line-height:1;
  }
  .modal-footer{flex-shrink:0;border-top:1px solid var(--card-border);background:var(--bg);}
  .modal-footer-row{
    display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:12px;
    padding:12px 24px;
  }
  .modal-footer-actions{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:14px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .modal-footer-nav{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;}
  .modal-footer-row .add-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;font-size:.85rem;white-space:nowrap;}
  .modal-footer-nav button{
    background:var(--navy);color:#fff;border:none;border-radius:10px;
    padding:8px 14px;font-size:.85rem;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
  }
  .modal-footer-nav button:hover:not(:disabled){background:#1c1e33;}
  .modal-footer-nav button:disabled{opacity:.3;cursor:default;}
  .modal-count{font-size:.8rem;color:var(--muted);white-space:nowrap;}
  .answer-box{
    margin-top:12px;background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--card-border);border-radius:8px;padding:12px;font-size:.85rem;
    white-space:pre-line;
  }
  .answer-toggle{
    border:none;background:var(--green);color:#fff;font-weight:700;font-size:.82rem;cursor:pointer;padding:8px 14px;border-radius:10px;
    width:112px;text-align:center;
  }
  .answer-toggle:hover{background:#00792f;}
  .modal-print-btn{
    border:none;background:var(--orange);color:#0f1120;font-weight:700;font-size:.82rem;cursor:pointer;padding:8px 14px;border-radius:10px;
  }

  @media print{
    /* Hide everything the shared layout adds around this page (header,
       footer, back-to-top button, whatever else lives directly in <body>)
       by only allowing our own wrapper through - more reliable than
       naming the layout's header/footer classes, which aren't visible
       from this file since they live in separate _includes partials. */
    body > *:not(#gqb-page){display:none !important;}
    .om-hero,.filters,.builder-bar,.card-actions,.results-meta,.load-more-wrap{display:none !important;}
    /* Printing must always show exactly what printSelected()/printOne()
       build from the grid cards - never the modal's own rendering (which
       uses a different, larger fill-width image scale). Without this, a
       print triggered from the popup's own "Print this question" button
       would show the modal's fixed-position content instead of, or on
       top of, the intended grid-card print output. */
    .modal-overlay{display:none !important;}
    .grid{display:block;}
    .card{
      display:block !important;
      border:1px solid #999;border-left:4px solid var(--strand,#999) !important;page-break-inside:avoid;margin-bottom:18px;
      height:auto !important;overflow:visible !important;
    }
    /* A higher-specificity selector is required here: .card already forces
       display:block !important above (needed so flexbox doesn't corrupt
       content across a page break - see .card-body note below), and an
       !important stylesheet rule beats a plain inline style, so printing
       used to silently override printSelected()/printOne()'s attempt to
       hide unchecked cards via c.style.display='none'. Hiding is done by
       toggling this class instead, whose compound selector outranks the
       single-class rule above regardless of !important on either side. */
    .card.print-hide{display:none !important;}
    /* Flexbox does not reliably fragment across a printed page break - when a
       card can't fit on one page whole (despite page-break-inside:avoid being
       only a hint), a flex column's children can render out of position or
       overlapping. Block layout fragments predictably, so the card's internal
       structure switches to plain block flow for print, with margins standing
       in for the on-screen flex gap. */
    .card-top{display:block !important;margin-bottom:8px;}
    .card-top > div{display:inline;}
    .card-top .subtopic-pill{display:inline-block;margin-right:8px;}
    .card-top .source-tag{display:inline;}
    .card-top .marks-badge{display:inline-block;float:right;}
    .card-body{display:block !important;overflow:visible !important;height:auto !important;}
    .card-body::after{display:none !important;}
    .q-heading{display:block;margin-bottom:8px;}
    .q-text{display:block;margin-bottom:10px;}
    .q-diagram{display:block !important;margin-bottom:10px;text-align:center;}
    .q-diagram img{display:inline-block !important;}
    .q-diagram.q-crop{text-align:left !important;}
    .q-diagram.q-crop img{display:block !important;margin:0 !important;}
    .answer-box{display:block;margin-top:10px;}
    body{background:#fff;}
    .print-answers.has-content{
      display:block !important;page-break-before:always;
    }
    .print-answers h2{font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif;font-weight:700;font-size:1.3rem;margin:0 0 16px;}
    .print-answers .answer-item{margin-bottom:16px;page-break-inside:avoid;}
    /* No separate "strong" rule needed here - .answer-box already styles
       the inline "Answer:"/"Mark scheme:" labels correctly on its own,
       matching the modal exactly. */
    .print-answers .answer-box{margin-top:4px;}
    .print-answers .answer-source{display:block;font-size:.78rem;color:#666;margin-bottom:4px;}
    /* All answers use the SAME (smaller) fraction size here, regardless of
       the on-screen large/small logic based on line length - a dense list
       of many answers together should read as one consistent size, not a
       mix, even though that per-line sizing is the right call on screen. */
    .print-answers .frac{font-size:.72em !important;line-height:.95 !important;margin:0 1px !important;}
    .print-answers .answer-item > div{white-space:pre-line;}
    /* .markscheme-text rule removed - mark scheme now lives inside
       .answer-box alongside "Answer:", matching the modal exactly. */
  }
</style>

<section class="om-hero" style="min-height:0; padding: 3.5rem 2rem 1.75rem;">
  <h1>GCSE maths <em>question bank</em></h1>
  <p>Search real Edexcel past paper questions by tier, paper, strand and sub-strand. View them on screen or print them straight into a worksheet.</p>
  <p style="margin-top:0.75rem;font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.75;">Past papers are the copyright of <a href="https://qualifications.pearson.com/en/qualifications/edexcel-gcses/mathematics-2015.html" style="color:inherit;">Pearson</a> and are provided here for revision purposes.</p>
</section>

<div class="filters">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="filter-row">
      <div class="filter-group">
        <span class="filter-label">Tier</span>
        <div class="tier-toggle" id="tierToggle">
          <button data-tier="all" class="active">All</button>
          <button data-tier="Foundation">Foundation</button>
          <button data-tier="Crossover">Crossover</button>
          <button data-tier="Higher">Higher</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="filter-group" style="margin-left:auto;">
        <span class="filter-label">Paper</span>
        <div class="tier-toggle" id="paperToggle">
          <button data-paper="all" class="active">All</button>
          <button data-paper="Paper 1 (non-calculator)">Paper 1 (non-calculator)</button>
          <button data-paper="Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)">Papers 2 &amp; 3 (calculator)</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="filter-row" style="margin-top:12px;">
      <div class="filter-group" style="width:100%;">
        <span class="filter-label">Strand</span>
        <div class="chip-row" id="strandChips"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="filter-row" style="margin-top:12px;justify-content:center;">
      <div class="filter-group" style="width:360px;max-width:100%;position:relative;">
        <div class="combobox">
          <input type="text" id="substrandInput" placeholder="Search or choose sub-strand" autocomplete="off">
          <button type="button" class="combobox-clear hidden" id="substrandClear" aria-label="Clear sub-strand filter">✕</button>
          <button type="button" class="combobox-arrow" id="substrandArrow" aria-label="Show all sub-strands">▾</button>
        </div>
        <div class="search-suggestions hidden" id="searchSuggestions"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="wrap">
  <div class="results-meta" id="resultsMeta"></div>
  <div class="grid" id="grid"></div>
  <div class="load-more-wrap" id="loadMoreWrap"></div>
</div>

<div class="builder-bar" id="builderBar">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="builder-left">
      <button class="btn btn-ghost" id="clearBtn">Clear selection</button>
      <div class="builder-info"><strong id="selCount">0</strong> questions selected &nbsp;·&nbsp; <span id="selMarks">0</span> marks total</div>
    </div>
    <div class="builder-actions">
      <label class="answers-toggle-label">
        <input type="checkbox" id="includeAnswersToggle">
        Include answers
      </label>
      <button class="btn btn-primary" id="printSelected">Print worksheet</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<div id="printAnswers" class="print-answers"></div>

<div class="modal-overlay hidden" id="modalOverlay">
  <div class="modal-box" id="modalBox">
    <button class="modal-close" id="modalClose">✕</button>
    <div class="modal-header" id="modalHeader"></div>
    <div class="modal-scroll-body" id="modalContent"></div>
    <div class="modal-footer">
      <div class="modal-footer-row">
        <div class="modal-footer-actions">
          <label class="add-label">
            <input type="checkbox" id="modalCheckbox">

// Scales an already-built <img> tag inline pixel width by a factor (used to show
// diagrams larger inside the wider question-viewer popup without duplicating image data).
function enlargeImg(html, factor){
  return html.replace(/width:(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)px/g, function(m,p1){ return "width:" + Math.round(parseFloat(p1)*factor) + "px"; });
}

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1FH-Q21",w:1045,h:990,needsHeading:false},n:"21",higherN:"1",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Statistics",subtopic:"Scatter graphs and correlation",marks:5,intro:"The scatter graph shows the maximum temperature and the number of hours of sunshine in fourteen British towns on one day.",svg:svgScatter,text:"One of the points is an outlier.\n(a) Write down the coordinates of this point.\n(b) For all the other points write down the type of correlation.\nOn the same day, in another British town, the maximum temperature was 16.4°C.\n(c) Estimate the number of hours of sunshine in this town on this day.\nA weatherman says,\n“Temperatures are higher on days when there is more sunshine.”\n(d) Does the scatter graph support what the weatherman says?\nGive a reason for your answer.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"(a) (10, 19)  (b) Positive correlation  (c) 12 to 13 hours  (d) Yes — the majority of points show that higher temperatures occur with more hours of sunshine (positive correlation)",markscheme:"(a) B1 cao — (10,19). (b) C1 positive (correlation). (c) M1 for an appropriate line of best fit drawn, or a point marked from 16.4 across to (x,16.4) where x is in range. A1 hours given in the range 12 to 13. (d) C1 (yes) e.g. as the majority of points show that for higher temperatures there is more sunshine (positive correlation)."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1FH-Q22",w:507,h:28,needsHeading:false},n:"22",higherN:"2",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Prime factorisation",marks:2,text:"Express 56 as the product of its prime factors.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"2 × 2 × 2 × 7 (= 2³ × 7)",markscheme:"M1 for complete method to find prime factors; could be seen as a factor tree with no more than 1 arithmetic error. A1 accept 2³ × 7. Answer: 2 × 2 × 2 × 7"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1FH-Q23",w:286,h:23,needsHeading:false},n:"23",higherN:"3",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Multiplying decimals",marks:3,text:"Work out 54.6 × 4.3",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"234.78",markscheme:"M1 for complete method with relative place value correct for two elements of the calculation, e.g. two lines of standard method or structure shown of partitioning method. A1 for digits 23478. A1 (ft dep M1) for correct placement of the decimal point. Answer: 234.78"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1FH-Q24",w:728,h:449,needsHeading:false},n:"24",higherN:"4",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Forming and showing equations",marks:3,svg:svgSquare,text:"The area of square <em>ABCD</em> is 10 cm².\nShow that <em>x</em>² + 6<em>x</em> = 1",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"Working: (x + 3)(x + 3) = 10 → x² + 6x + 9 = 10 → x² + 6x = 1 (shown)",markscheme:"M1 writes the area using algebraic terms e.g. (x+3) × (x+3), which may be written on the diagram or x given as √10 − 3. M1 expands and includes the given 10, e.g. x² + 3x + 3x + 9 = 10 when expanding, or 10 − 3√10 − 3√10 + 9 + 6√10 − 18 for the surd approach. A1 rearranges to give the given equation, or shows surd equivalent. Conclusion: x² + 6x = 1 (shown)"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1FH-Q25",w:1045,h:325,needsHeading:false},n:"25",higherN:"5",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Pythagoras and perimeter",marks:5,intro:"This rectangular frame is made from 5 straight pieces of metal.",svg:svgFrame,text:"The weight of the metal is 1.5 kg per metre.\nWork out the total weight of the metal in the frame.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"70.5 kg",markscheme:"P1 starts process of Pythagoras e.g. 5² + 12². P1 complete process for Pythagoras e.g. √(5²+12²) (=13). P1 (dep on Pythagoras) process of adding all the lengths (5+12+13+5+12=47). P1 (indep) process of multiplying at least 2 lengths by 1.5. A1 cao. Answer: 70.5 kg. SC: any evidence of working with Pythagoras award at least P1."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1FH-Q26",w:505,h:93,needsHeading:false},n:"26",higherN:"6",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Parallel lines and gradients",marks:2,text:"The equation of the line <em>L</em>₁ is <em>y</em> = 3<em>x</em> − 2\nThe equation of the line <em>L</em>₂ is 3<em>y</em> − 9<em>x</em> + 5 = 0\nShow that these two lines are parallel.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"Both lines have gradient 3 (L₂ rearranges to y = 3x − 5/3), so the lines are parallel",markscheme:"M1 starts to manipulate expression e.g. 3y = 9x − 5 or 3y − 9x = −5. A1 gives equation(s) which can be used to show the gradients are equal, e.g. y = 3x − 5/3, so both lines have gradient 3, hence parallel."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1F-Q27",w:1047,h:663,needsHeading:false},n:"27",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Vectors",marks:3,svg:svgVectors,text:"<em>ABCD</em> is a parallelogram.\nThe diagonals of the parallelogram intersect at <em>O</em>.\n<span class=\"vec\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 40 14\"><line x1=\"1\" y1=\"7\" x2=\"34\" y2=\"7\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/><polygon points=\"34,7 26,2 26,12\" fill=\"currentColor\"/></svg><em>OA</em></span> = <strong>a</strong> and <span class=\"vec\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 40 14\"><line x1=\"1\" y1=\"7\" x2=\"34\" y2=\"7\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/><polygon points=\"34,7 26,2 26,12\" fill=\"currentColor\"/></svg><em>OB</em></span> = <strong>b</strong>\n(a) Find, in terms of <strong>b</strong>, the vector <span class=\"vec\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 40 14\"><line x1=\"1\" y1=\"7\" x2=\"34\" y2=\"7\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/><polygon points=\"34,7 26,2 26,12\" fill=\"currentColor\"/></svg><em>DB</em></span>.\n(b) Find, in terms of <strong>a</strong> and <strong>b</strong>, the vector <span class=\"vec\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 40 14\"><line x1=\"1\" y1=\"7\" x2=\"34\" y2=\"7\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/><polygon points=\"34,7 26,2 26,12\" fill=\"currentColor\"/></svg><em>AB</em></span>.\n(c) Find, in terms of <strong>a</strong> and <strong>b</strong>, the vector <span class=\"vec\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 40 14\"><line x1=\"1\" y1=\"7\" x2=\"34\" y2=\"7\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/><polygon points=\"34,7 26,2 26,12\" fill=\"currentColor\"/></svg><em>AD</em></span>.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"(a) 2b  (b) b − a  (c) −a − b",markscheme:"(a) B1 oe — 2b. (b) B1 oe — b − a. (c) B1 ft oe — −a − b."},

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q7",w:458,h:149,needsHeading:false},n:"H7",tier:"Higher",strand:"Statistics",subtopic:"Averages (mean)",marks:3,text:"There are 10 boys and 20 girls in a class.\nThe class has a test.\nThe mean mark for all the class is 60\nThe mean mark for the girls is 54\nWork out the mean mark for the boys.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"72",markscheme:"P1 for showing the process of 30 × 60 (=1800) or 20 × 54 (=1080). P1 (dep P1) for showing the complete process e.g. (1800 − 1080) ÷ 10. A1 concluding the answer is 72 (and not 66)."},
 {n:"H8",tier:"Higher",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Standard form",marks:3,qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q8",w:569,h:186,needsHeading:false},paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"(a) 0.00000797 (b) 6.3 × 10⁷",markscheme:"(a) B1 cao. Answer: 0.00000797 (b) M1 for partial calculation involving powers of 10 e.g. 0.63 × 10⁸ or for 63000000. A1 cao. Answer: 6.3 × 10⁷"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q9",w:815,h:126,needsHeading:false},n:"H9",tier:"Higher",strand:"Ratio, proportion and rates of change",subtopic:"Reverse percentages",marks:2,text:"Jules buys a washing machine.\n20% VAT is added to the price of the washing machine.\nJules then has to pay a total of £600\nWhat is the price of the washing machine with <strong>no</strong> VAT added?",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"£500",markscheme:"M1 recognition of 1.2 or 120% oe e.g. 600 ÷ 1.2 oe. A1 cao. Answer: £500"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q10",w:819,h:56,needsHeading:false},n:"H10",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Expanding brackets (cubic)",marks:3,text:"Show that (<em>x</em> + 1)(<em>x</em> + 2)(<em>x</em> + 3) can be written in the form <em>ax</em>³ + <em>bx</em>² + <em>cx</em> + <em>d</em>\nwhere <em>a</em>, <em>b</em>, <em>c</em> and <em>d</em> are positive integers.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"x³ + 6x² + 11x + 6",markscheme:"M1 for method to find the product of any two linear expressions, e.g. x²+x+2x+2 or x²+2x+3x+6 or x²+x+3x+3. M1 for method of multiplying out remaining products, having already found one correctly. A1 cao. Answer: x³+6x²+11x+6"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q11",w:1045,h:944,needsHeading:false},n:"H11",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Graphs of quadratic functions",marks:3,intro:"The graph of <em>y</em> = <em>f</em>(<em>x</em>) is drawn on the grid.",svg:svgH11Graph,text:"(a) Write down the coordinates of the turning point of the graph.\n(b) Write down estimates for the roots of <em>f</em>(<em>x</em>) = 0\n(c) Use the graph to find an estimate for <em>f</em>(1.5)",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"(a) (1, −3)  (b) −0.75, 2.75 (accept −0.7 to −0.8 and 2.7 to 2.8)  (c) −2.8",markscheme:"(a) B1 cao — (1,−3). (b) B1 accept −0.7 to −0.8 and 2.7 to 2.8 — (−0.75, 2.75). (c) B1 cao — (−2.8)."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q12",w:349,h:235,needsHeading:false},n:"H12",tier:"Higher",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Fractional and negative indices",marks:4,text:"(a) Find the value of 81<span class=\"exp\">−<span class=\"frac\"><span class=\"num\">1</span><span class=\"den\">2</span></span></span>\n\n(b) Find the value of (64/125)<span class=\"exp\"><span class=\"frac\"><span class=\"num\">2</span><span class=\"den\">3</span></span></span>",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"(a) 1/9  (b) 16/25",markscheme:"(a) M1 for showing a method using either reciprocal or square root of 81. A1 cao — accept 1/9 or 0.1 recurring. (b) M1 for showing cube root of 64 as 4 and cube root of 125 as 5, or 16/n (n≠25) or 25/n (n≠16) or an intention to find (4/5)². A1 cao — accept 0.64."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q13",w:866,h:482,needsHeading:false},n:"H13",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Direct and inverse proportion",marks:4,intro:"The table shows a set of values for <em>x</em> and <em>y</em>.",svg:svgH13Table,text:"<em>y</em> is inversely proportional to the square of <em>x</em>.\n(a) Find an equation for <em>y</em> in terms of <em>x</em>.\n(b) Find the positive value of <em>x</em> when <em>y</em> = 16",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"(a) y = 9/x²  (b) x = 3/4",markscheme:"(a) M1 begins to work with y = k/x² oe e.g. substitution of a pair of number values to find k. A1 for y = 9/x² (accept y = 9x⁻²). (b) M1 ft (dep on previous M1) substitutes y=16 into their proportionality equation and rearranges. A1 oe. Answer: x = 3/4"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q14",w:827,h:224,needsHeading:false},n:"H14",tier:"Higher",strand:"Ratio, proportion and rates of change",subtopic:"Ratio (nested/combined)",marks:4,text:"White shapes and black shapes are used in a game.\nSome of the shapes are circles.\nAll the other shapes are squares.\nThe ratio of the number of white shapes to the number of black shapes is 3:7\nThe ratio of the number of white circles to the number of white squares is 4:5\nThe ratio of the number of black circles to the number of black squares is 2:5\nWork out what fraction of all the shapes are circles.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"1/3",markscheme:"P1 process to solve the problem e.g. 3:7 with 4:5 → 12:15:21 or working towards a common multiple of the ratios. P1 second step of the process e.g. 7:2 with the black ratio converted to a common scale. P1 for complete process combining all three given ratios into one set of parts. A1 for 1/3 oe."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q15",w:1045,h:451,needsHeading:false},n:"H15",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Volume of cones and estimation",marks:4,intro:"A cone has a volume of 98 cm³.\nThe radius of the cone is 5.13 cm.\n(a) Work out an estimate for the height of the cone.",svg:svgCone,text:"John uses a calculator to work out the height of the cone to 2 decimal places.\n(b) Will your estimate be more than John's answer or less than John's answer?\nGive reasons for your answer.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"(a) 3.5 to 4.5 cm (accept range)  (b) More — since the numerator (98) was rounded up and this increases the calculated height",markscheme:"(a) M1 substitution into formula ⅓πr²h with chosen estimate values and starts rearrangement e.g. multiplies by 3, divides by π and r². M1 uses estimates in calculation e.g. 3×100/3×25 (or in rearranged form). A1 arrives at a single value from estimate, in the range 3.5 to 4.5. (b) C1 ft e.g. more, since the numerator (98, rounded up) being used means the calculated height is larger than the true height."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q16",w:722,h:63,needsHeading:false},n:"H16",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Algebraic proof",marks:4,text:"<em>n</em> is an integer greater than 1\nProve algebraically that <em>n</em>² − 2 − (<em>n</em> − 2)² is always an even number.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"n² − 2 − (n − 2)² = 4n − 6 = 2(2n − 3), which is always even since it's a multiple of 2 (proof shown)",markscheme:"C1 correct expansion of brackets to give at least 3 terms of (n−2)². C1 arrives at n²−2−n²+4n−4 oe. C1 reduces to 2(2n−3) or 4n−6. C1 for conclusion e.g. 2(2n−3) is always even since 2× any integer is always a multiple of 2."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q17",w:707,h:184,needsHeading:false},n:"H17",tier:"Higher",strand:"Probability",subtopic:"Probability without replacement",marks:4,text:"There are 9 counters in a bag.\n7 of the counters are green.\n2 of the counters are blue.\nRia takes at random two counters from the bag.\nWork out the probability that Ria takes one counter of each colour.\nYou must show your working.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"28/72 (= 7/18)",markscheme:"P1 for 6/8 or 2/8 or 7/8 or 1/8 oe seen on a diagram or in a calculation. P1 for 7/9 × 2/8 or 2/9 × 7/8 or 14/72 oe. P1 for 7/9×2/8 + 2/9×7/8 oe, or for 1 − (7/9×6/8 + 2/9×1/8) oe. A1 oe. Answer: 28/72 (=7/18). SC B1 for 14/81, B2 for 28/81."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q18",w:772,h:550,needsHeading:false},n:"H18",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Equations of straight lines (shapes)",marks:4,svg:svgRhombus,text:"<em>ABCD</em> is a rhombus.\nThe coordinates of <em>A</em> are (5, 11)\nThe equation of the diagonal <em>DB</em> is <em>y</em> = ½<em>x</em> + 6\nFind an equation of the diagonal <em>AC</em>.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"y = −2x + 21",markscheme:"P1 shows evidence of understanding that AC is perpendicular to DB, e.g. gradient of DB is ½ so gradient of AC is −2 (negative reciprocal). P1 shows a process to find the gradient of a perpendicular line, e.g. states y=−2x+c or states the gradient of AC as −2. P1 (dep on P2) for substitution of x=5, y=11 into y=mx+c with their gradient. A1 oe. Answer: y = −2x + 21"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q19",w:814,h:530,needsHeading:false},n:"H19",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Vectors",marks:4,svg:svgOABC,text:"<em>OABC</em> is a parallelogram.\n<span class=\"vec\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 40 14\"><line x1=\"1\" y1=\"7\" x2=\"34\" y2=\"7\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/><polygon points=\"34,7 26,2 26,12\" fill=\"currentColor\"/></svg><em>OA</em></span> = <strong>a</strong> and <span class=\"vec\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 40 14\"><line x1=\"1\" y1=\"7\" x2=\"34\" y2=\"7\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/><polygon points=\"34,7 26,2 26,12\" fill=\"currentColor\"/></svg><em>OC</em></span> = <strong>c</strong>\n<em>X</em> is the midpoint of the line <em>AC</em>.\n<em>OCD</em> is a straight line so that <em>OC</em> : <em>CD</em> = <em>k</em> : 1\nGiven that <span class=\"vec\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 40 14\"><line x1=\"1\" y1=\"7\" x2=\"34\" y2=\"7\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/><polygon points=\"34,7 26,2 26,12\" fill=\"currentColor\"/></svg><em>XD</em></span> = 3<strong>c</strong> − ½<strong>a</strong>\nfind the value of <em>k</em>.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"k = 2/5",markscheme:"P1 for first step to solve the problem e.g. AC = −a+c oe, showing location of D and X on the diagram. P1 for a correct vector statement using CD, e.g. CD = 2.5c oe. P1 for a correct equation or ratio using k, e.g. equating XD found two ways or OD:OC = (k+1):k oe. A1 cao. Answer: k = 2/5"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q20",w:592,h:91,needsHeading:false},n:"H20",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Simultaneous equations (quadratic)",marks:5,text:"Solve algebraically the simultaneous equations\n<em>x</em>² + <em>y</em>² = 25\n<em>y</em> − 3<em>x</em> = 13",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"x = −24/5, y = 7/5  and  x = −3, y = 4",markscheme:"M1 for substitution of a rearrangement of y−3x=13 (y=3x+13) into x²+y²=25. M1 (dep M1) for expansion of the bracket after substitution, e.g. x²+9x²+78x+169. M1 for forming a quadratic ready for solving e.g. 10x²+78x+144=0. M1 for factorising e.g. (5x+24)(x+3)(=0) oe. A1 x=−24/5, y=7/5 and x=−3, y=4. SC: B1 (if M0) for all 4 values mis-associated or one correct pair of coordinates."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q21",w:755,h:317,needsHeading:false},n:"H21",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Geometric proof",marks:4,intro:"<em>ABCD</em> is a quadrilateral.",svg:svgTrapProof,text:"<em>AB</em> = <em>CD</em>.\nAngle <em>ABC</em> = angle <em>BCD</em>.\nProve that <em>AC</em> = <em>BD</em>.",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"Proof: AB = CD (given), angle ABC = angle BCD (given), BC = BC (common) → triangle ABC ≡ triangle DCB (SAS) → AC = BD",markscheme:"C1 states angle ABC = angle BCD (given). C1 states 2nd link AB = CD (given). C1 states 3rd link with reason: BC = BC (common). C1 concludes proof by stating triangle ABC ≡ triangle DCB (SAS), so AC = BD."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-1H-Q22",w:792,h:569,needsHeading:false},n:"H22",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Trigonometry (advanced proof)",marks:5,intro:"The diagram shows a hexagon <em>ABCDEF</em>.",svg:svgHexagon,text:"<em>ABEF</em> and <em>CBED</em> are congruent parallelograms where <em>AB</em> = <em>BC</em> = <em>x</em> cm.\n<em>P</em> is the point on <em>AF</em> and <em>Q</em> is the point on <em>CD</em> such that <em>BP</em> = <em>BQ</em> = 10 cm.\nGiven that angle <em>ABC</em> = 30°,\nprove that cos(<em>PBQ</em>) = 1 − <span class=\"frac\"><span class=\"num\">(2 − √3)</span><span class=\"den\">200</span></span><em>x</em>²",paper:"Paper 1 (non-calculator)",answer:"Proof using the cosine rule on triangle PBQ, with cos 30° = √3/2, shows cos(PBQ) = 1 − ((2 − √3)/200)x²",markscheme:"B1 (indep) for stating cos 30° = √3/2. M1 for PQ² = 10²+10²−2×10×10×cos(PBQ) using the cosine rule. M1 for cos(PBQ) = (10²+10²−PQ²)/(2×10×10), implying the previous line. M1 for cos(PBQ) = (10²+10²−(2x²−2x²cos30°))/200 or equivalent substitution. A1 conclusion of proof with all working seen: cos(PBQ) = 1 − ((2−√3)/200)x²"},

 {n:"3",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Statistics",subtopic:"Bar charts",marks:5,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q3",w:1047,h:958,needsHeading:false},paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"(a) Walk (b) A bar of height 7 is drawn for girls in the 'Walk' category.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q4",w:749,h:144,needsHeading:false},n:"4",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Ordering fractions",marks:2,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Here are four fractions.\n2/5   11/30   1/2   7/15\nWrite these fractions in order of size.\nStart with the smallest fraction.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"11/30, 2/5, 7/15, 1/2",markscheme:"M1 for converting all fractions to a common denominator of 30 (12/30, 11/30, 15/30, 14/30).  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q5a",w:772,h:368,needsHeading:false},svg:tblTallyCDs,n:"5(a)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Statistics",subtopic:"Data collection (tally charts)",marks:1,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"David sells CDs in a shop. The tally chart shows information about the number of CDs David sold on Monday, on Tuesday and on Wednesday.",text:"(a) Write down one thing that is wrong with the tally chart.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"The tally marks for Monday show 13 (two full groups of 5 plus 3) but the frequency is recorded as 12, so the tally and frequency don't match.",markscheme:"B1 for an appropriate criticism, e.g. the tally for Monday does not match the stated frequency of 12."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q5b",w:932,h:240,needsHeading:true},svg:tblPictogramCDs,n:"5(b)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Statistics",subtopic:"Data collection (pictograms)",marks:1,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"David drew this pictogram to show the information for Tuesday and Wednesday.\n(b) Write down one thing that is wrong with this pictogram.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"Tuesday only shows 5 circles (5 × 3 = 15), but the frequency was 18 — an extra circle is needed.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q6",w:819,h:177,needsHeading:false},n:"6",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Fractions and percentages of amounts",marks:4,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"There are 495 coins in a bottle.\n1/3 of the coins are £1 coins.\n124 of the coins are 50p coins.\nThe rest of the coins are 20p coins.\nWork out the total value of the 495 coins.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"£268.20",markscheme:"M1 for 495 ÷ 3 (=165) £1 coins.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q10",w:928,h:303,needsHeading:false},svg:boxEnvelopePrices,n:"10",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Best value",marks:4,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"Suha is going to buy 150 envelopes. C1 for correct conclusion: Letters2send, with correct supporting figures."},

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q16",w:737,h:763,needsHeading:false},svg:svgLociMap,n:"16",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Loci and construction",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"A, B and C are three points on a map, drawn at a scale of 1 cm to 100 metres.\nPoint T is 250 metres from point A.\nPoint T is equidistant from point B and point C.",text:"On the map, show one of the possible positions for point T.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"T lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC, at the point(s) where a circle of radius 2.5 cm centred on A crosses that bisector.",markscheme:"M1 for a circle, radius 2.5 cm (±2 mm), centre A.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2FH-Q17",w:952,h:221,needsHeading:false},svg:tblDiceProb,n:"17",higherN:"1",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Probability",subtopic:"Relative frequency",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"The table shows the probabilities that a biased dice will land on 2, on 3, on 4, on 5 and on 6\nNumber on dice: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\nProbability: —, 0.17, 0.18, 0.09, 0.15, 0.1",text:"Neymar rolls the biased dice 200 times.\nWork out an estimate for the total number of times the dice will land on 1 or on 3",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"98",markscheme:"M1 for 1 − (0.17+0.18+0.09+0.15+0.1) (=0.31) to find P(1). M1 for P(1)+P(3) (=0.31+0.18=0.49). A1 for 200×0.49. Answer: 98"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2FH-Q18",w:726,h:273,needsHeading:false},n:"18",higherN:"2",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Ratio, proportion and rates of change",subtopic:"Ratio and percentages combined",marks:5,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"On Saturday, some adults and some children were in a theatre.\nThe ratio of the number of adults to the number of children was 5 : 2\nEach person had a seat in the Circle or had a seat in the Stalls.\n3/4 of the children had seats in the Stalls.\n117 children had seats in the Circle.\nThere are exactly 2600 seats in the theatre.\nOn this Saturday, were there people on more than 60% of the seats?\nYou must show how you get your answer.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"Yes — 1638 seats were occupied, which is more than 60% of 2600 (1560).",markscheme:"M1 for recognising 117 represents 1/4 of the children (since 3/4 are in Stalls). M1 for 117÷1/4 (=468) children. M1 for 468×5/2 (=1170) adults. M1 for 468+1170 (=1638) total people. C1 for comparing 1638 with 60% of 2600 (=1560) and concluding Yes."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2FH-Q19",w:988,h:1166,needsHeading:false},svg:svgPrismTrapezium,n:"19",higherN:"3",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Plans and elevations",marks:4,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"The diagram shows a prism with a cross section in the shape of a trapezium, with dimensions 2 m, 2 m, 0.5 m, 0.5 m, 2.5 m and 1 m marked as shown.",text:"On the centimetre grid, draw the front elevation and the side elevation of the prism.\nUse a scale of 2 cm to 1 m.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"Side elevation: a 4 cm by 2 cm rectangle (representing 2 m by 1 m) with a solid line drawn 1 cm in from the 2 cm edge. Front elevation: a trapezium with base 4 cm, parallel sides 1 cm and 4 cm (representing the trapezium cross-section, base 2 m, parallel sides 0.5 m and 2 m).",markscheme:"C2 for the side elevation (4 cm by 2 cm rectangle with a solid line drawn 1 cm from the 2 cm edge, correct orientation). [C1 for the side elevation as a rectangle.] C2 for the front elevation as a trapezium in correct orientation with base 4 cm, parallel sides 1 cm and 4 cm. [C1 for the front elevation as a trapezium with two right angles.]"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2FH-Q20a",w:1045,h:149,needsHeading:false},n:"20(a)",higherN:"4(a)",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Ratio, proportion and rates of change",subtopic:"Speed, distance, time",marks:4,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Olly drove 56 km from Liverpool to Manchester.\nHe then drove 61 km from Manchester to Sheffield.\nOlly's average speed from Liverpool to Manchester was 70 km/h.\nOlly took 75 minutes to drive from Manchester to Sheffield.\n(a) Work out Olly's average speed for his total drive from Liverpool to Sheffield.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"57.1 km/h (3 sf)",markscheme:"M1 for 56÷70 (=0.8 hours) time for first leg. M1 for 75÷60 (=1.25 hours) time for second leg. M1 for (56+61)÷(0.8+1.25). A1 cao. Answer: 57.1 km/h (accept 57 km/h)"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2FH-Q20b",w:894,h:184,needsHeading:true},n:"20(b)",higherN:"4(b)",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Ratio, proportion and rates of change",subtopic:"Speed, distance, time (reasoning)",marks:1,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Janie drove from Barnsley to York.\nJanie's average speed from Barnsley to Leeds was 80 km/h.\nHer average speed from Leeds to York was 60 km/h.\nJanie says that the average speed from Barnsley to York can be found by working out the mean of 80 km/h and 60 km/h.\n(b) If Janie is correct, what does this tell you about the two parts of Janie's journey?",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"The two parts of the journey (Barnsley to Leeds and Leeds to York) must have taken the same amount of time.",markscheme:"C1 for a correct statement, e.g. the time taken for each part of the journey must be equal."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2FH-Q21",w:1045,h:739,needsHeading:false},n:"21",higherN:"5",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Similar triangles",marks:4,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",svg:`<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Question 21, cropped directly from the original exam paper" style="aspect-ratio:1030 / 542;width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;display:block;margin:0 auto;">`,text:"",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"(a) AE = 3.9 cm  (b) AB = 2.05 cm",markscheme:"(a) M1 for recognising triangle ECA is similar to triangle DCB and using the scale factor EC/DC (=1.5). A1 cao — AE = 3.9 cm. (b) M1 for finding BC using the similar triangles ratio, e.g. BC = AC×DC/EC (=4.1). A1 for AB = AC − BC = 2.05 cm."},
 
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2FH-Q22",w:928,h:287,needsHeading:false},n:"22",higherN:"6",tier:"Crossover",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Compound interest",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"Anil wants to invest £25 000 for 3 years in a bank.\nPersonal Bank: Compound Interest, 2% for each year\nSecure Bank: Compound Interest, 4.3% for the first year, 0.9% for each extra year",text:"Which bank will give Anil the most interest at the end of 3 years?\nYou must show all your working.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"Secure Bank gives (slightly) more interest — £26 546.46 (Secure) vs £26 530.20 (Personal), a difference of about £16.26.",markscheme:"M1 for 25000×1.02³ (=26530.20). M1 for 25000×1.043×1.009×1.009 (=26546.46). C1 for correct comparison and conclusion: Secure Bank gives more interest (by about £16.26)."},

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q8",w:924,h:877,needsHeading:false},svg:svgCumFreqHeights,n:"H8",tier:"Higher",strand:"Statistics",subtopic:"Cumulative frequency",marks:2,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"The cumulative frequency graph shows some information about the heights, in cm, of 60 students.",text:"Work out an estimate for the number of these students with a height greater than 160 cm.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"12 (accept 11.8 to 12.2)",markscheme:"M1 for evidence of taking a reading from the graph at h = 160 and subtracting from 60.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q9",w:840,h:879,needsHeading:false},svg:svgReflectTriangleA,n:"H9",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Transformations (reflections)",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"Triangle A is drawn on a grid.\nKyle reflects triangle A in the x-axis to get triangle B, then reflects triangle B in the line y = x to get triangle C.\nAmy reflects triangle A in the line y = x to get triangle D, then reflects triangle D in the x-axis to get triangle E.\nAmy says that triangle E should be in the same position as triangle C.",text:"Is Amy correct?\nYou must show how you get your answer.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"No — reflecting in the x-axis then in y = x is equivalent to a 90° anticlockwise rotation about O, while doing the reflections in the reverse order (Amy's route) gives a 90° clockwise rotation, so C and E end up in different positions.",markscheme:"M2 for correctly finding the position of C or D (M1 for a correct position of B or D). C1 for No with correct supporting evidence, e.g. showing C and E in the correct (different) positions, or stating C is a rotation of 90° anticlockwise about O while E is a rotation of 90° clockwise about O."},

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q11",w:819,h:56,needsHeading:false},n:"H11",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Solving equations (algebraic fractions)",marks:4,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Solve (3<em>x</em> − 2)/4 − (2<em>x</em> + 5)/3 = (1 − <em>x</em>)/6",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"x = 28/3",markscheme:"M1 for multiplying every term by 12 (the LCM of 4, 3 and 6).  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q12a",w:1045,h:730,needsHeading:false},svg:svgProbTree,n:"H12(a)",tier:"Higher",strand:"Probability",subtopic:"Tree diagrams",marks:1,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"There are 30 students in Mr Lear's class. 16 of the students are boys.\nTwo students from the class are chosen at random.\nMr Lear draws a probability tree diagram for this information, showing 16/30 then 15/30 and 14/30 for the second boy/girl branches, and 14/30 then 16/30 and 13/30 for the second branches after girl.",text:"(a) Write down one thing that is wrong with the probabilities in the probability tree diagram.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"After the first student is chosen there are only 29 students left, so the second-pick denominators should be 29, not 30 (e.g. it should be 15/29, not 15/30).",markscheme:"B1 for identifying that the denominators for the second pick should be 29 (since it's without replacement), not 30."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q12b",w:889,h:225,needsHeading:true},n:"H12(b)",tier:"Higher",strand:"Probability",subtopic:"Combined events",marks:1,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Owen and Wasim play for the school football team.\nThe probability that Owen will score a goal in the next match is 0.4\nThe probability that Wasim will score a goal in the next match is 0.25\nMr Slater says, 'The probability that both boys will score a goal in the next match is 0.4 + 0.25'\n(b) Is Mr Slater right?\nGive a reason for your answer.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"No — for independent events you multiply the probabilities (0.4 × 0.25), you don't add them; adding is used for 'either... or', not 'both'.",markscheme:"C1 for 'No' with a correct reason, e.g. probabilities for independent events happening together should be multiplied, not added."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q13",w:951,h:888,needsHeading:false},svg:svgHistogramAges,n:"H13",tier:"Higher",strand:"Statistics",subtopic:"Histograms",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"The histogram shows some information about the ages of the 134 members of a sports club, with frequency density bars for age bands 0–10, 10–20, 20–40, 40–60 and 60–90.\n20% of the members of the sports club who are over 50 years of age are female.",text:"Work out an estimate for the number of female members who are over 50 years of age.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"7",markscheme:"P1 for a correct process to find any frequency, e.g. frequency density × class width for part of the 40–60 bar or the 60–90 bar. P1 (dep) for the complete process to find 20% of the total frequency for over-50s. A1 cao. Answer: 7"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q14",w:988,h:1273,needsHeading:false},n:"H14",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Graphs of functions",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"Nine graphs, labelled A to I, are shown.",text:"In the table, match each equation with the letter of its graph.\n<em>y</em> = sin <em>x</em>\n<em>y</em> = <em>x</em>³ + 4<em>x</em>\n<em>y</em> = 2<span class=\"exp\"><em>x</em></span>\n<em>y</em> = 4/<em>x</em>",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"y = sin x → C; y = x³ + 4x → F; y = 2^x → A; y = 4/x → H (verify letters against the actual printed graphs)",markscheme:"B1 for each correct match, up to 3 marks (allow follow-through consistent with the actual graphs shown)."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q15",w:796,h:668,needsHeading:false},svg:svgCircleABCDE,n:"H15",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Circle theorems / similar triangles",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"A, B, C and D are four points on the circumference of a circle.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q16",w:652,h:56,needsHeading:false},n:"H16",tier:"Higher",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Recurring decimals to fractions",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Using algebra, prove that 0.1(36 recurring) × 0.(2 recurring) is equal in value to 1/33",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"0.1(36) = 3/22 and 0.(2) = 2/9.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q17",w:1045,h:546,needsHeading:false},svg:svgSectorONQ,n:"H17",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Sectors and area",marks:5,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"ONQ is a sector of a circle with centre O, angle NOQ = 60° and radius 11 cm. A1 for an answer in the range 66.5 to 66.6."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q18",w:353,h:67,needsHeading:false},n:"H18",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Indices (fractional)",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"16<span class=\"exp\"><span class=\"frac\"><span class=\"num\">1</span><span class=\"den\">5</span></span></span> × 2<span class=\"exp\"><em>x</em></span> = 8<span class=\"exp\"><span class=\"frac\"><span class=\"num\">3</span><span class=\"den\">4</span></span></span>\nWork out the exact value of <em>x</em>.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"x = 29/20",markscheme:"M1 for writing 16 and 8 as powers of 2 (16=2⁴, 8=2³).  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q24",w:296,h:23,needsHeading:false},n:"24",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Solving quadratic equations (factorising)",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Solve <em>x</em>² + 5<em>x</em> − 24 = 0",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"x = −8, x = 3",markscheme:"M1 for factorising or substituting into the quadratic formula, (x±a)(x±b) where the product of a and b is 24, e.g. (x±4)(x±6), or the difference of a and b is 5, e.g. (x±2)(x±7). M1 for (x+8)(x−3). A1 cao. Answer: x = −8, x = 3 — this question is missing from the original PDF extraction of the question paper; wording and answer confirmed against the official mark scheme and a separate scanned copy of the paper."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q25a",w:819,h:92,needsHeading:false},n:"25(a)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Sequences (linear nth term)",marks:2,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"Here are the first six terms of an arithmetic sequence.\n3   8   13   18   23   28",text:"(a) Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"5n − 2",markscheme:"B2 for 5n − 2 oe.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2F-Q25b",w:535,h:119,needsHeading:true},n:"25(b)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Sequences (quadratic nth term)",marks:1,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"The nth term of a different sequence is 3n²\nNathan says that the 4th term of this sequence is 144\n(b) Is Nathan right?\nShow how you get your answer.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"No — 3 × 4² = 48, not 144. (144 would come from squaring 3n first, i.e. (3×4)², rather than squaring n first.)",markscheme:"C1 for No with evidence, e.g. 3 × 4² = 48, 48 ≠ 144, he has multiplied by 3 first but should have squared first — this question is missing from the original PDF extraction of the question paper; wording and answer confirmed against the official mark scheme and a separate scanned copy of the paper."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q19",w:819,h:120,needsHeading:false},n:"H19",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Algebraic fractions",marks:4,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"2 − (<em>x</em> + 2)/(<em>x</em> − 3) − (<em>x</em> − 6)/(<em>x</em> + 3) can be written as a single fraction in the form (<em>ax</em> + <em>b</em>)/(<em>x</em>² − 9)\nwhere a and b are integers.\nWork out the value of a and the value of b.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"a = 4, b = −42",markscheme:"M1 for writing all three terms over a common denominator of (x−3)(x+3). M1 for correctly expanding the numerators. A1 for a = 4. A1 for b = −42"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q20a",w:924,h:812,needsHeading:false},svg:svgQuadraticGraph,n:"H20(a)",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Graphs (quadratic)",marks:2,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"The diagram shows part of the graph of y = x² − 2x + 3",text:"(a) By drawing a suitable straight line, use your graph to find estimates for the solutions of x² − 3x − 1 = 0",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"x ≈ 3.3 or x ≈ −0.3 (exact values (3±√13)/2)",markscheme:"M1 for rearranging to identify the line y = x + 4 needs to be drawn (since x²−2x+3 = x+4 rearranges to x²−3x−1=0). A1 for both solutions in the range 3.2 to 3.4 and −0.2 to −0.4."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q20b",w:924,h:824,needsHeading:false},n:"H20(b)",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Graphs (gradient estimation)",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"P is the point on the graph of y = x² − 2x + 3 where x = 2\n(b) Calculate an estimate for the gradient of the graph at the point P.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"2 (accept 1.8 to 2.2, from drawing a tangent at P)",markscheme:"M1 for drawing a tangent to the curve at x = 2. M1 for calculating the gradient of the tangent, e.g. using two points on it. A1 for an answer in the range 1.8 to 2.2 (exact value 2, from differentiating: dy/dx = 2x − 2)."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q21",w:1045,h:491,needsHeading:false},svg:svgThreeCirclesRect,n:"H21",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Circles in shapes",marks:4,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"The diagram shows 3 identical circles inside a rectangle (two circles side by side along the top, one circle beneath them). Each circle touches the other two circles and the sides of the rectangle. The radius of each circle is 24 mm.",text:"Work out the area of the rectangle.\nGive your answer correct to 3 significant figures.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"8600 mm² (accept 8592 to 8602)",markscheme:"P1 for the length of the rectangle, e.g. 24×4 (=96, i.e. 2 diameters). P1 for the perpendicular height of the equilateral triangle formed by the circle centres (side 48 mm), e.g. 48sin60° (≈41.57). P1 for the width of the rectangle, e.g. 41.57+24+24 (≈89.57). A1 for an answer in the range 8592 to 8602."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q22",w:732,h:459,needsHeading:false},n:"H22",tier:"Higher",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Sequences (quadratic)",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Here are the first five terms of a sequence.\n4   11   22   37   56\nFind an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"2n² + n + 1",markscheme:"M1 for finding the second difference (=4) and halving to get the n² coefficient (2). M1 for setting up simultaneous equations using two terms to find the linear part. A1 cao. Answer: 2n² + n + 1"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-2H-Q23",w:554,h:145,needsHeading:false},n:"H23",tier:"Higher",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Circle equations and tangents",marks:3,paperNum:"2",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"L is the circle with equation <em>x</em>² + <em>y</em>² = 4\nP(3/2, √7/2) is a point on L.\nFind an equation of the tangent to L at the point P.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"3x + √7y = 8",markscheme:"M1 for finding the gradient of the radius OP (=√7/3). M1 for the perpendicular (tangent) gradient (=−3/√7 or −3√7/7). A1 for a correct equation of the tangent, e.g. 3x + √7y = 8"},

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q1a",w:728,h:384,needsHeading:false},svg:tblRivers,n:"1(a)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Ordering numbers",marks:1,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"The table shows the lengths of five rivers.\nTrent: 297 km, Don: 112 km, Severn: 354 km, Thames: 346 km, Mersey: 113 km",text:"(a) Write down the rivers in order of length.\nStart with the shortest river.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"Don, Mersey, Trent, Thames, Severn",markscheme:"B1 cao, all five in correct order."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q1b",w:881,h:424,needsHeading:false},n:"1(b)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Multiplicative reasoning",marks:1,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Ami says, 'The River Thames is more than three times as long as the River Don.'\n(b) Show that Ami is correct.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"3 × 112 = 336, and 346 > 336, so the Thames is more than three times as long as the Don.",markscheme:"B1 for 3×112 (=336) compared with 346, and 346>336 stated."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q2",w:920,h:161,needsHeading:false},n:"2",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Forming expressions",marks:2,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Cups are sold in packs and in boxes.\nThere are 12 cups in each pack.\nThere are 18 cups in each box.\nAlison buys p packs of cups and b boxes of cups.\nWrite down an expression, in terms of p and b, for the total number of cups Alison buys.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"12p + 18b",markscheme:"M1 for 12p or 18b seen. A1 cao. Answer: 12p + 18b"},
 {n:"3",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Place value",marks:2,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q3",w:982,h:348,needsHeading:false},paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"(i) 15 (ii) 195",markscheme:"(i) B1 cao. Answer: 15 (ii) B1 cao. Answer: 195"},

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q5a",w:558,h:124,needsHeading:false},n:"5(a)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Ratio, proportion and rates of change",subtopic:"Ratio from fractions",marks:1,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"A path is made of white tiles and grey tiles.\n1/4 of the tiles are white.\n(a) Write down the ratio of white tiles to grey tiles.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"1 : 3",markscheme:"B1 cao.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q5b",w:558,h:154,needsHeading:false},n:"5(b)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Ratio, proportion and rates of change",subtopic:"Ratio problems",marks:2,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"There is a total of 56 tiles.\n(b) Work out the number of grey tiles.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"42",markscheme:"M1 for 56÷4×3 or equivalent.  {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q6a",w:798,h:219,needsHeading:false},n:"6(a)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Statistics",subtopic:"Averages (median)",marks:1,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"Here is a list of numbers.\n12   15   14   17   22   19   13\nBridgit says, 'To work out the median you find the middle number, so the median of these numbers is 17.'\nBridgit's answer is not correct.",text:"(a) What is wrong with Bridgit's method?",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"Bridgit didn't put the numbers in order first — sorted, the list is 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 19, 22, so the median (middle value) is actually 15, not 17.",markscheme:"C1 for identifying that the numbers must be put in ascending (or descending) order before finding the middle value."},

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q7",w:762,h:300,needsHeading:false},n:"7",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Probability",subtopic:"Systematic listing",marks:2,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"Priti is going to have a meal. She can choose one starter and one main course from the menu.\nStarter: Salad, Fish, Melon\nMain Course: Pasta, Rice, Burger",text:"Write down all the possible combinations Priti can choose.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"Salad+Pasta, Salad+Rice, Salad+Burger, Fish+Pasta, Fish+Rice, Fish+Burger, Melon+Pasta, Melon+Rice, Melon+Burger (9 combinations)",markscheme:"M1 for at least 6 correct combinations listed systematically. A1 for all 9 correct combinations, no repeats."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q8",w:815,h:156,needsHeading:false},n:"8",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Money problems",marks:2,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"Joanne wants to buy a dishwasher.\nThe dishwasher costs £372\nJoanne will pay a deposit of £36\nShe will then pay the rest of the cost in 4 equal monthly payments.\nHow much is each monthly payment?",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"£84",markscheme:"M1 for 372 − 36 (=336). A1 for 336÷4=84. Answer: £84"},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q9",w:917,h:506,needsHeading:false},svg:tblCleaningTimes,n:"9",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Number",subtopic:"Time calculations",marks:3,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"Davos is a cleaner. The table shows information about the time it will take him to clean each of four rooms in a house.\nKitchen: 2 hours; Sitting room: 1 hour 40 minutes; Bedroom: 1½ hours; Bathroom: 45 minutes\nDavos wants to clean all four rooms in one day. He will have breaks for a total time of 75 minutes.\nDavos is going to start cleaning at 9 am.",text:"Will he finish cleaning by 4 pm?\nYou must show all your working.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"No — total time needed = 120+100+90+45 = 355 minutes cleaning, plus 75 minutes of breaks = 430 minutes (7 hours 10 minutes), so starting at 9 am he finishes at 4:10 pm, which is after 4 pm.",markscheme:"M1 for adding the four cleaning times in consistent units (=355 minutes). M1 for adding the 75 minutes of breaks (=430 minutes total). A1 for converting to 7 hours 10 minutes and adding to the 9 am start time. C1 for correct conclusion: No, he finishes at 4:10 pm."},
 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q10",w:1045,h:185,needsHeading:false},n:"10",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Geometry and measures",subtopic:"Ratio on a line",marks:3,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",intro:"ABC is a straight line. The length AB is five times the length BC. AC = 90 cm.",text:"Work out the length AB.",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"75 cm",markscheme:"M1 for recognising AC is split into 6 equal parts (5 for AB, 1 for BC). M1 for 90÷6 (=15). A1 for AB = 5×15 = 75 cm."},

 {qimg:{src:"Sum2017-3F-Q11b",w:514,h:28,needsHeading:true},n:"11(b)",tier:"Foundation",strand:"Algebra",subtopic:"Rearranging formulae",marks:2,paperNum:"3",sitting:"Summer 2017",text:"(b) Make v the subject of the formula T = 4v + 3",paper:"Papers 2 & 3 (calculator)",answer:"v = (T − 3)/4",markscheme:"M1 for T − 3 = 4v.
